sentence: This project studies which genetic changes in prostate cancers are linked to ancestry and aggressive disease, using sequencing and organoid models made from prostate tissue.
This project tries to discover scientific principles and develop immunotherapies for the treatment of cancers in children.
This project builds software tools that compare how genes are regulated in healthy tissue and diseased tissue, using sequencing of individual cells.
This project uses a knockout mouse model to find out which organs are harmed in a deficiency disease and whether vitamin B3 therapy helps.
This project studies how a protein that senses mechanical stretch affects the working of the kidney tubule in health and disease.
This project uses biochemistry and mass spectrometry of proteins to find out how cells control iron metabolism when iron availability changes.
This project develops ways to do MRI with an open magnet that can be made in any shape or size.
This project studies the roles of RNA modification in how the nervous system develops and works, using mouse and human brain organoid models.
This project uses humanized mouse models and single-cell RNA sequencing to find out how HIV persists in the central nervous system.
This project uses machine learning and multi-omic methods to find better ways to detect pulmonary hypertension in patients with pulmonary fibrosis.
This project tests a natural small molecule that blocks how HIV integrase interacts with a host factor and viral RNA, to limit drug resistance.
This project develops and maintains cell lines, genetically engineered mouse models and patient-derived xenografts for studying resistance to treatment.
This project develops tools to detect and track implanted cells and tissues in pigs in a non-invasive way.
This project studies how chromatin proteins that are often mutated in human cancers work together and change chromatin to control transcription.
This project uses pain tests, biomechanics and machine learning to find different types of carpometacarpal osteoarthritis.
This project studies the genetic causes of stillbirth and fetal structural anomalies by combining large genomic and clinical datasets.
This project tests whether noise-induced hearing loss harms decision-making by disrupting connections between the auditory and parietal cortices.
This project builds human models of Alzheimer's disease from pluripotent stem cells, using ways to make glial cells and nerve cells age.
This project uses two kinds of sequencing and CRISPR editing in retinal organoids to find non-coding variants that cause Usher disease.
This project builds a flat-panel detector that takes two x-ray images at once at different energies to improve breast cancer detection.
